references.text: God had previously given Balaam permission to go with the men, but only to say what God commanded him.
Balaam confirms that he can only speak what the Lord puts in his mouth.
Balaam repeats that he can only do what the Lord says.
Balaam declares that he cannot go beyond the Lord's command, neither for good nor for evil.
A prophet shall speak what God puts in his mouth, the same principle that applies to Balaam.
The prophet Micah confirms the same principle: he can only say what the Lord says to him.
Jeremiah is instructed to speak all that God commands him, corresponding to Balaam's mission.
Ezekiel receives a similar command to speak God's words to the people.
